channel.title: Paper Pulse
channel.description: Keyword-based research paper aggregation from arXiv and IACR

item.title: DTRU: A Versatile, Compact, Simple, and Robust NTRU KEM with Double $E_8$ Encoding
item.description:
## Overview This paper introduces **DTRU**, a versatile NTRU-based KEM designed to meet China's 2025 commercial cryptographic standards (128/256/512-bit security).
## Key Contributions - **Double $E_8$ encoding** constructs 16-dimensional lattice codes with low decoding complexity, improving error correction and reducing bandwidth. - Supports multiple ring structures (power-of-two cyclotomic, tricyclotomic, and LPPNF) for flexibility. - Deliberately simple: avoids coefficient compression and redundant invertibility checks, enabling code reuse on low-power devices. - Security is ensured via parameter redundancy, LPPNF risk mitigation, and non-sparse noise distributions.
## Results Comprehensive implementations (C, AVX2, ARM) show DTRU is **49–52% more compact** and **3.84–15.69× faster** than NTRU-HRSS, and **7–27% more compact** and **1.05–1.32× faster** than Kyber at equivalent security levels.
## Impact DTRU offers a balanced, practical alternative for post-quantum KEM deployment, particularly in constrained environments.

item.title: Qlapoty: Improved analysis and eﬃciency for quaternionic ideal to isogeny transformation
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper addresses critical flaws in the Qlapoti algorithm for quaternionic ideal-to-isogeny transformation, a key component of the SQIsign post-quantum signature scheme. We correct the failure probability analysis, resolve discrepancies between the original pseudocode and its implementation, and propose a **new norm equation solver** with negligible failure probability.
## Results & Impact Our C implementation achieves **6–9× speedup** over Qlapoti’s norm equation solver, and **1.3–2.1× faster** end-to-end SQIsign NIST2 signatures across different security levels. These improvements make the scheme more practical for real-world deployment while maintaining rigorous mathematical guarantees. The work bridges a critical gap between theoretical analysis and engineering practice in isogeny-based cryptography.

item.title: DumboMix: Robust Asynchronous Anonymous Broadcast Made Practical
item.description:
## DumboMix: Practical Robust Asynchronous Anonymous Broadcast
We present **DumboMix**, a practical framework for asynchronous anonymous broadcast with guaranteed output delivery (robustness), enabling $n$ servers to privately collect $N$ messages from clients and reveal them in a uniformly random order, despite up to $n/3$ Byzantine faults and network asynchrony.
**Core contribution**: We design two efficient arithmetic circuits (DumboMix1 & DumboMix2) for mixing in Shamir-secret-shared MPC, requiring only $\mathcal{O}(1)$ multiplicative depth, $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ scalar multiplications, and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ MPC multiplications—outperforming prior art (Blinder, butterfly networks, RabbitMix, PowerMix) in both complexity and functionality.
**Implementation & results**: Integrated into DumboMPC++ (an optimized robust AMPC framework), our circuits achieve **44.8–65.9×**, **4.8–7.1×**, and **2.7–4.0×** speedups over RabbitMix, PowerMix, and butterfly switching networks respectively when shuffling 1024 messages in LAN (37.1–52.7×, 3.9–5.5×, 5.1–7.2× in WAN), with $n$ from 4 to 31 servers.

item.title: MamaBearZKP: A Holistic Co-design of Prime Fields and Proving Stacks for High-Throughput ZKP on Modern CPUs
item.description:
## Core Contribution **MamaBearZKP** presents a holistic co-design framework that unifies prime field arithmetic, protocol structure, and CPU hardware primitives to maximize ZKP throughput on modern processors. The key enabler is a novel 49-bit prime field (MamaBear, $p = 2^{49} - 2^{34} + 1$), whose arithmetic headroom permits efficient lazy reduction and enables high-performance fused fold-and-evaluate kernels under the AVX-512IFMA execution model.
## Key Results Instantiated in a HyperPlonk-DeepFold prover, MamaBearZKP achieves **up to 42×/33×/15×/21×/21× single-thread speedups** for ZeroCheck, ProductCheck, DeepFold Commit, DeepFold Open, and end-to-end proving, respectively, over a Goldilocks-based baseline. With 8 threads, these gains reach **64×/47×/81×/45×/45×**. Compared to Plonky3 (already using AVX-512 BabyBear), it delivers up to **18× single-thread end-to-end speedup**.
## Insight These gains arise from a synergistic cascade: the 49-bit field enables lazy reduction, which unlocks efficient fused kernels, which in turn support a unified stay-packed dataflow across the entire proving stack—this end-to-end design is what converts AVX-512IFMA's raw throughput into realized performance.

item.title: Actively Secure Two-Party Function Secret Sharing with Dynamic Cross-Phase Verification
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **VeriFSS**, the first dealer-free two-party function secret sharing scheme with active security, proven in the standard simulation framework against one static malicious corruption. The construction introduces a **two-plane key** binding generation transcripts, computed functions, and released shares via a secret global authentication scalar, eliminating the need for vector commitments or per-point interaction.
## Key Results - **Provable security**: Two novel lemmas—moment-fidelity (error $3/|E|$) and shape-identification ($2n/|E|$)—establish cross-phase binding in any field characteristic, with a Galois-ring variant for $\mathbb{Z}_{2^k}$ payloads. - **Efficiency**: Generation costs 2 rounds and 5 field elements per party per level; certification adds $O(n)$ elements independent of domain size, with constant-round dynamic aggregation for heterogeneous instances. - **Experimental validation**: At $n=16$, certified DPF generation takes 5.7 ms, certification 3.3 ms, with keys only 5.4% larger than the semi-honest baseline. Aggregated certification traffic converges to 1,282 bytes/instance; a 50 ms RTT session completes in 1.15 s regardless of batch size. - **Attack resilience**: All 1,400 injected deviations rejected (six classes perfectly; the seventh exactly matches the modeled single-bit selective-failure predicate), confirming the security proof quantitatively.

item.title: Toward Secure Compilation: Leakage Detection for Masked Implementations in Jasmin
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces a **leakage detection pass** for the Jasmin compiler, operating on its intermediate representation *before* register and stack allocation, within its formally verified pipeline.
## Method & Result Instead of power-trace simulation, the pass employs a **configurable microarchitecture-oriented leakage model** that tracks contact between shares, secrets, randomness, and public values, making root causes explicit and enabling detection of masking-order reductions. Validation on **60 dedicated test snippets** covering all leakage sources confirms its effectiveness.
## Significance This work bridges the gap between source-level verification and post-compilation hardware leakage, laying the foundation for an automatic leakage-removal stage—a concrete step toward **secure compilation**.

item.title: On the Impossibility of Robust Combiners for Cryptographic Groups
item.description: This paper initiates the study of robust combiners for cryptographic groups in Maurer's generic group model (GGM), where algorithms access group elements only via abstract algebraic operations. A $(k,n)$-robust combiner merges $n$ candidate groups into one that remains secure if at least $k$ are secure. The authors establish two fundamental impossibility results: (1) for the decisional Diffie-Hellman (DDH) assumption, no generic $(k,n)$-robust combiner exists for any $k<n$; (2) for the discrete logarithm (DLog) problem, robust combination is possible only when the combined group order is large enough to encode secrets of $n-k+1$ components, with a tight threshold at $\log N \ge (n-k+1)\lambda$. Conversely, if $\log N \le (n-k)\lambda$, no generic secure combiner exists. These results reveal that decisional assumptions cannot be robustly combined in the GGM, while search assumptions achieve robustness only at essentially optimal representation cost. Consequently, robustness for group-based cryptography must generally be realized at higher layers, such as protocol design or key derivation.

item.title: Relations Between the Uniform MQ Assumption and Other Multivariate Assumptions
item.description:
## Core Contributions This paper investigates the logical relations among three multivariate quadratic (MQ) assumptions: the **Uniform MQ (UMQ)** assumption, the **MQ one-wayness (MQOW)** assumption, and the **MQ second-preimage resistance (MQSPR)** assumption.
## Key Results We establish the following tight reductions: 1. **UMQ ⇔ MQSPR**: These two assumptions tightly imply each other. 2. **MQOW ⇒ UMQ**: This implication is tight. 3. **UMQ ⇒ MQOW** under the parameter condition **m ≤ n + O(log λ)**, where n is the number of variables, m is the number of equations, and λ is the security parameter. The reduction becomes tight when m ≤ n + O(1).
## Main Corollary and Significance As a direct consequence, **MQSPR implies MQOW** under the same condition m ≤ n + O(log λ), which is considerably weaker than the compression condition n = m + ω(log λ) required for general function families. Our result covers both the square case (m = n) and mildly overdetermined systems (m = n + O(log λ)). This is the first systematic treatment of these inter-relations, providing finer theoretical tools for security proofs of MQ-based cryptographic schemes.

item.title: The ePrint:2026/1591 Quantum Algorithm Does Not Solve DCP
item.description:
## Core Result This note formally refutes Simon's algorithm (ePrint:2026/1591) for the Dihedral Coset Problem (DCP). We prove that the algorithm **cannot extract the least-significant bit of the DCP secret** with non-negligible advantage, hence it does not solve DCP.
## Key Findings - **Broad No-Go Theorem**: Our result extends beyond Simon's specific algorithm to a general class of DCP algorithms following Regev's reduction template. We show that any such algorithm must make **extensive use of classical Fourier labels** during the uncomputation stage. - **Information-theoretic Failure**: Simon's algorithm uses only the **most-significant third** of the Fourier labels (within error $\mathsf{poly}(n)2^{-n/3}$), which we prove is insufficient to determine the secret's least-significant bit. - **Formal Verification**: We provide complete Lean 4 proof code at: https://github.com/sragavan99/lean-ePrint-2026-1591-refutation.
## Significance This work provides crucial design guidance for future DCP algorithms and demonstrates the value of formal methods in cryptographic algorithm analysis.

item.title: From Round Skipping to S-Box Skipping: Attacking Poseidon's Partial Layer via Subspace Restriction
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **GSR**, a generalized S-box skipping gadget that absorbs one initial full round and \(t-2k\) partial rounds of Poseidon without increasing polynomial degree. By restricting the solution subspace of total constraints—independent of round constants and MDS matrix—the method linearizes internal transitions, reducing an infeasible polynomial system to a bounded low-degree ideal parameterized by \(k\) free variables.
## Key Results - Constructed a **probability-1 distinguisher** for \(t-2k+1\) rounds, enabling interpolation-based attacks. - Solved **CICO-1 over 28/31 rounds** and **CICO-2 over 25/31 rounds** in the Ethereum Poseidon setting (KoalaBear field, \(t=24\), \(\alpha=3\)). - The attack applies universally to any Poseidon variant, as it depends only on \(t\) and \(k\), not on constants, MDS, exponent, or field size.
This work extends round-skipping to S-box-level skipping, demonstrating that structural parameters—not concrete choices—determine Poseidon's algebraic security.

item.title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils
item.description:
## Core Contribution This study introduces an **uncertainty-aware deep learning framework** for sex attribution in Upper Paleolithic hand stencils, explicitly modeling and propagating uncertainty through dual image/contour processing, structured silhouette augmentation, and ensemble aggregation.
## Key Results Using two ensembles of ten deep networks (EfficientNet-B3 and MobileViT-S) trained on 14,036 contemporary hand samples, the framework achieves >88% accuracy on older age groups. A triangulated validation scheme integrating ensemble predictions, UMAP latent-space mapping, and LayerCAM attributions ensures anatomical consistency.
## Significance Applied to prehistoric stencils, the framework yields both sex predictions and internal confidence measures, distinguishing stable from ambiguous cases. Convergence across predictions, latent structure, and interpretability demonstrates that uncertainty can serve as a measurable component of archaeological inference, enabling robust decoding of ancient rock art.

item.title: RecipeNet: A Hierarchical Transformer for Recipe Data
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **RecipeNet**, a hierarchical Transformer that jointly models intra-step field interactions and inter-step sequential dependencies via two stacked encoder levels. Unlike flat tabular methods, it preserves the inherent structure of recipe data (ordered steps with heterogeneous fields).
## Key Results Experiments across multiple recipe datasets (materials, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing) show RecipeNet **consistently outperforms** existing tabular baselines on various prediction tasks. Ablation studies confirm both hierarchical and sequential modeling are crucial for performance.
## Significance This work provides a more natural representation learning framework for procedural data, bridging tabular learning and sequence modeling—a valuable direction for process-intensive domains.

item.title: Rollplex: Cross-Phase GPU Spatial Sharing for Vision Language Model Post-Training
item.description:
## Core Contribution Rollplex is a runtime system that enables **cross-phase GPU spatial sharing** for vision-language model (VLM) post-training. It identifies that prefix computation—which processes dense video inputs and prompt tokens—is independent of response generation, yet current on-policy RL runtimes execute rollout, reference scoring, and training in strict serial phases, leaving GPU compute underutilized.
## Key Mechanisms Rollplex decomposes reference/training phases and overlaps prefix computation with rollout decoding. To handle the 165 GiB/GPU memory requirement of naive colocation, it introduces: (1) **phase-aware memory management** that controls HBM residency via producer-consumer lifetimes, and (2) **parallelism-aware weight sharing** that reuses physical storage for layout-compatible tensors across different tensor-parallel degrees, avoiding a full second actor copy.
## Results On 32 H800 GPUs, Rollplex achieves **1.23×–1.30× speedup** over serial colocation and **1.57×–2.24× speedup** over disaggregation under the same GPU budget, while preserving synchronous RL update semantics. This demonstrates that significant efficiency gains are possible without altering RL algorithm behavior, offering a practical system-level optimization for large-scale multimodal RL training.

item.title: Generating Benchmark Health Data Using a Tabular Diffusion Transformer
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper proposes a **two-stage cross-tabular data generation (CTDG) framework** that overcomes the single-table limitation of existing methods. The first stage converts heterogeneous raw tables into standardized statistical tables with uniform columns, capturing marginal distributions and pairwise correlations. The second stage trains a **tabular diffusion transformer** to learn structural patterns across these homogeneous statistical tables and generate synthetic ones, from which raw tables are reconstructed via Gaussian sampling and inverse probability integral transform.
## Key Results The framework enables learning a unified generative model from multiple heterogeneous tables and supports unlimited synthetic table generation. Experiments demonstrate **high statistical fidelity** and a **favorable fidelity-diversity trade-off**, validating the effectiveness of this approach for benchmark health data generation and broader CTDG applications.

item.title: LP-NAS: Linear Programming-based Neural Architecture Search
item.description:
## Core Contribution We propose **LP-NAS**, a mathematical programming framework for differentiable neural architecture search. It formulates a linear program using validation-loss gradients and training-loss Hessian to derive architecture update directions that improve generalization while preserving parameter optimality. Two efficient variants, S-LP-NAS and R-LP-NAS, are introduced and instantiated as S-LP-DARTS and R-LP-DARTS in the DARTS search space.
## Key Results Both variants achieve faster convergence and significantly higher validation performance in early search iterations than standard DARTS. On CIFAR-10/100, LP-DARTS outperforms standard DARTS in both search and evaluation phases. Comparisons with P-DARTS, PC-DARTS, and STO-DARTS on CIFAR-10 confirm its effectiveness, and ImageNet experiments demonstrate the transferability of discovered architectures.
## Impact LP-NAS bridges linear programming and NAS, offering a theoretically grounded, computationally efficient approach for rapid architecture exploration, particularly beneficial in early-stage optimization and resource-constrained settings.

item.title: Designing Compact Neural Architectures via Neuron Gating and Mixed Activation
item.description: This paper proposes a general bilevel optimization framework for neural architecture search (NAS) across MLPs, CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers, targeting compact yet high-performance architectures. Three continuous relaxation formulations—neuron gating (NAS-NG), mixed activation (NAS-MA), and their combination (NAS-NGMA)—replace discrete architectural decisions with differentiable surrogates, enabling scalable optimization over combinatorial spaces. On MNIST and CIFAR-10, the methods consistently find compact architectures with competitive or improved accuracy: e.g., NAS-NGMA achieves 98.68% (MLP) and NAS-NG reaches 99.63% (CNN) on MNIST, while all outperform vanilla DARTS on CIFAR-10. Notably, NAS-NG can also refine over-parameterized or literature-optimal architectures, reducing parameters while boosting accuracy. This establishes relaxed bilevel optimization as a scalable alternative to discrete NAS and offers a general tool for neuron- and activation-level architecture search.

item.title: Style or Signature? Artist-Disjoint Evaluation of Style Classification in Frozen Vision Embeddings
item.description:
## Core Contribution We demonstrate that high style-classification accuracy in frozen vision embeddings (e.g., CLIP) largely reflects **artist recognition**, not genuine style understanding. Standard random splits leak artist identity across train/test sets, enabling classifiers to shortcut by identifying painters.
## Method & Key Results We introduce an **artist-disjoint evaluation protocol** that holds out all works by each artist. On 320 paintings from four 20th-century movements, 5-NN style accuracy drops from 0.87 to 0.77. The decline is sharply uneven: Impressionism and Cubism remain stable, while Surrealism falls by 20 points. This pattern persists across four encoders, including a vision-only self-supervised model, confirming the effect is visual, not linguistic.
## Conclusion Artist-disjoint evaluation is **necessary** to measure true stylistic generalization. Our findings expose a fundamental limitation of current embedding benchmarks and highlight that some movements (e.g., Surrealism) lack robust shared visual form, making them inherently harder to classify by style alone.

item.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View
item.description: This paper unifies fragmented RL post-training methods for diffusion models under a single **path-space principle**. By applying importance sampling between sampling SDEs to the regularized diffusion-RL objective, the authors derive an explicit policy-gradient estimator that bridges reverse-trajectory methods (e.g., Flow-GRPO) and forward-matching methods (e.g., AWM, DiffusionNFT), revealing their empirical gap as a **variance-reduction effect** rather than a conceptual difference. The derivation yields a unified design space organized by value-gradient estimation, weight functions, and sampling choices, within which they propose a multi-sample KDE value-gradient estimator and scale-bounded weight families. Experiments on SD3.5-M and Qwen-Image validate the variance-reduction explanation and demonstrate consistent improvements over prior diffusion-RL baselines.

item.title: CytoBERT: A Foundation Model for Cytometry Data
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **CytoBERT**, the first open-source foundation model for single-cell cytometry data with variable marker panels. Pretrained on a curated corpus of 15 heterogeneous human datasets (50M+ cells) via self-supervised learning, it captures transferable inter-marker relationships within cells.
## Key Results Fine-tuning CytoBERT for sample-level classification demonstrates that cross-dataset transfer learning is feasible despite experimental heterogeneity. The model achieves robust generalization across diverse marker panels, providing a scalable and reproducible baseline for cytometry analysis. All code and weights are publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: Offline Deep Q* Estimation with Diffusion Models
item.description:
## Offline Deep Q* Estimation with Diffusion Models
This paper addresses offline reinforcement learning by estimating the optimal action-value function Q* through solving the Bellman equation with unknown reward and transition dynamics. We propose a novel framework that decouples operator estimation from value learning: conditional diffusion models first estimate the reward law and transition kernel, inducing a data-driven optimal Bellman operator, which is then plugged into a deep Q* estimator via empirical Bellman residual minimization. Theoretically, we establish sharp nonasymptotic convergence rates for operator learning in total variation distance, derive the oracle residual risk of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(n^{-2\beta/(d_x+d_a+2\beta)})$, and obtain an $L^2$ convergence rate of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(n^{-\beta/(d_x+d_a+2\beta)})$ for the final estimator under a concentrability condition—all without completeness assumptions. Extensive experiments confirm the method's strong empirical performance.

item.title: Boosting Data Augmentation with Stochastic Weight Averaging
item.description: ## Core Contribution This paper investigates **Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA)** as a cost-efficient alternative to deep ensembles for exploiting task symmetries via data augmentation. By approximating the late-training trajectory with an **Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process**, the authors theoretically demonstrate that in the infinite-width limit, SWA on augmented data yields an **equivariance boost** beyond the performance gain from SWA alone. Extensive experiments across vision and graph classification tasks with both discrete and continuous symmetries confirm the theoretical predictions. This work establishes SWA as a practical tool for achieving symmetry-aware models without repeated training runs, offering significant computational savings while enhancing generalization through better symmetry incorporation.

item.title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty of Delay Detection in Business Processes
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper investigates the intrinsic difficulty of delay detection in business processes, challenging the common focus on aggregate prediction metrics.
## Key Findings Across 14 event logs, we reveal that remaining times are strongly right-skewed, with models performing well on typical cases but poorly on high-delay ones. We further uncover pronounced heteroscedasticity—predictive uncertainty grows with delay magnitude.
## Method & Implication Mitigation strategies for class imbalance yield limited gains, suggesting the core issue is not imbalance but higher uncertainty. We exploit this correlation to substantially improve delayed-case identification, advocating uncertainty-aware modeling as a promising direction for future predictive process monitoring research.

item.title: ATLAS: Discovering Agent Strategies through LLM-Guided Abstraction and Automata Learning
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **ATLAS**, a framework that combines trace abstraction with automata learning to recover interpretable finite-state behavioral models from LLM-based agent trajectories. Unlike existing evaluations focused on task success, ATLAS explicitly captures agent-environment interaction strategies.
## Key Results Applied to a penetration-testing agent across 12 vulnerable machines, ATLAS revealed high-level attack strategies—such as decision points, success paths, and failure loops—that are invisible in raw execution traces. The learned symbolic models also enable knowledge transfer from frontier models to compact language models, and support model-transformation-based generation of concise behavioral explanations.
## Significance ATLAS demonstrates a novel model-driven engineering opportunity: transforming opaque agent trajectories into explicit, analyzable behavioral models, thereby enabling systematic auditing, explainability, and guided exploration of autonomous AI systems.

item.title: Non-Parametric Spatiotemporal Trajectory Prediction via State-Conditioned Transition Sampling
item.description: This paper introduces a **training-free, non-parametric** approach for multi-modal trajectory prediction that rivals a 57M-parameter transformer in accuracy while requiring zero GPU and no learned parameters. The method constructs a transition table of historical state-to-next-position pairs and retrieves neighbors via a product kernel over spatial proximity, bearing, speed, and temporal context. Two inference modes—diversity-penalized sampling and beam search—operate on this shared representation. On the TrAISformer maritime benchmark, our method achieves competitive accuracy with full data and remains stable down to 10% of training data, where the transformer degrades catastrophically. This enables deployment in new regions with an order of magnitude less historical data and no training cost, offering a practical alternative for data-scarce trajectory forecasting.

item.title: CORAL: Curriculum-Optimized Reward Adaptation for LiDAR-Based Goal-Directed Urban Driving
item.description:
## Core Contribution CORAL introduces a **dual-schedule co-optimization** framework to address the ordering challenge in multi-objective long-horizon urban driving.
## Method - **Five-stage curriculum**: progressively extends route length (100→150m) and tightens behavioral constraints - **Stage-aware reward**: dynamically shifts weight emphasis from mission progress to route following, safety, smoothness, and rule compliance
## Key Results - **100% success rate** on longest routes with full constraints (PPO baselines: 5-10%) - Ablation: removing either schedule drops success to ≤55%, proving their complementarity - **Zero-shot transfer** to 7 unseen towns: 68-98% success, mean lateral deviation <0.35m
## Technical Highlights - Compact 99-dim state: polar LiDAR histogram + telemetry + ego-frame route + traffic-rule indicators (no point-cloud encoder or BEV rasterization) - Multi-stream actor-critic trained with PPO in CARLA

item.title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **Principle-Bench**, the first benchmark covering four evaluation axes—accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration—for LLM-as-judge in principle-based regulation. It contains 168 cryptoasset financial-promotion scenarios mapped to two UK FCA principles, with pre-registered perturbations including paraphrases, adversarial keyword-stuffing, and boundary cases.
## Key Innovation We propose **Ceca (Calibrated Exemplar-Cluster Assessment)**, an auditable assessor that provides per-exemplar counterfactual attributions, enhancing transparency in LLM-based regulatory evaluation.
## Major Findings No method dominates all four axes. A 120B LLM-judge, strongest on benign inputs, drops 47 accuracy points (0.74→0.27) on keyword-stuffed Consumer Duty inputs—a clear case of "compliance theatre." A second judge from a different model family agrees only at κ=0.16 on that split, localizing the failure to the model rather than the corpus.
## Recommendation Deployment-grade LLM-judges for principle-based regulation must report per-principle adversarial deception rates and post-hoc calibration alongside aggregate accuracy.

item.title: Quantum Multi-Armed Bandits and Linear Bandits: Lower Bounds and Algorithms
item.description: This paper studies quantum multi-armed bandits (QMAB) and quantum linear bandits (QLB) under the oracle model of Wan et al. (2023). We prove the first minimax lower bounds: Ω(K log(T/K)) for QMAB and Ω(d log(T/d)) for finite-action QLB, resolving whether T-independent regret is achievable. Our proof hinges on a high-confidence single-arm quantum testing lower bound, established via the polynomial method and a Remez-type inequality for trigonometric polynomials, followed by bandit-to-testing reductions. Complementing these bounds, we design a design-based elimination algorithm for finite-action QLB achieving regret linear in d (when action set size is poly(d)), improving the prior d² dependence and matching our lower bound up to polylog factors. The algorithm couples a low-bias low-variance quantum mean estimator with a small-support G-optimal design, reducing dimension dependence from d² to d^{3/2} with quantum Monte Carlo estimates, and further to d via variance-based error aggregation.

item.title: Intelligent Detection of Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Metrics Based on 2D Floor Plans
item.description:
## Core Contribution This study introduces a Mask R-CNN-based model to automatically extract MEP metrics from 2D floor plans, focusing on lighting symbol detection, type classification, and associated text recognition. The model achieves strong performance with a bbox_mAP of 0.7596 and segm_mAP of 0.7111, and demonstrates robustness across IoU thresholds (bbox_mAP@50: 0.9850; segm_mAP@75: 0.9219).
## Significance This work enables efficient floor plan design and power estimation, directly benefiting architecture and construction industries by reducing manual inspection time. It also serves as a foundational step toward automated energy-efficient building design tools. The high accuracy under varied IoU conditions validates its practical applicability for real-world MEP object detection.

item.title: Detecting Contaminated Code-Generation Prompt Batches via Influence Functions
item.description: **CodeSIFT** is a threat-model-agnostic detection method that leverages influence functions to identify contaminated code-generation prompt batches. Instead of detecting specific vulnerabilities, it measures the parameter-space influence of generated code and applies a statistical test to flag deviations from benign reference distributions. Evaluated on two new benchmark datasets across three open-weight code LLMs (3B–7B parameters), CodeSIFT achieves AUROC scores up to 0.98 at moderate-to-high injection rates, with well-calibrated false positive rates and substantial gains over static analysis baselines. This work demonstrates that influence-function-based detection offers a promising defense against malicious code-generation prompts without requiring prior knowledge of the attack class.

item.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present a **differential fault-injection validation method** for LLM-modernized scientific software. The harness instruments 12 sites in GAMESS's shared SCF driver, applying identical deterministic faults (transient bit-flips, persistent perturbations, reduced precision) to both original Fortran and LLM-converted implementations, isolating the integral kernels.
## Key Results Across 2,200+ runs, transient-fault absorption costs match a contraction-based model (predicted slopes 0.74/1.49 iterations per bit vs. measured 0.82/1.50), and persistent perturbations halve energy error per extra bit. The campaigns exposed phase-dependent parallel deadlocks and false convergence under reduced precision—invisible to nominal testing. Critically, **all 200 paired injections** showed identical behavior between original and modernized kernels, and a measurement-guided synchronization fix composed correctly in all 40 additional pairs.
## Significance This is the first systematic differential fault-injection framework for validating LLM-based code modernization, providing quantitative fault-response models and revealing failure modes that standard validation misses.

item.title: Large-scale workflow placement in serverless computing using integer nonlinear programming
item.description: ## Core Contribution This paper tackles the **large-scale workflow placement problem** in serverless edge computing by formulating it as a **nonlinear integer program (INLP)** that jointly minimizes user monetary cost and workflow execution time. To overcome scalability issues and handle partially distributed node information, a **novel decomposition strategy** is proposed. Case studies demonstrate the approach's superior scaling properties and a **mean improvement of 10%** over a simple deployment heuristic, offering a practical and mathematically rigorous solution for optimizing resource allocation in heterogeneous cloud/edge environments.

item.title: Could Model Partitioning Make Federated Learning More Sustainable?
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **model partitioning** as a novel mechanism for reducing the carbon footprint of federated learning (FL), particularly in cross-silo deployments. Instead of merely shrinking client models, the proposed approach dynamically **offloads partial model layers** to other participants based on carbon-intensity or grid-load signals, thereby shifting energy consumption to greener or less strained contexts.
## Key Results Preliminary evaluations demonstrate that at certain partition points, model partitioning can cut a participant's local energy consumption by **up to 76%**, with **no significant time or energy overhead** compared to non-partitioned training. This suggests that partitioning offers a flexible and efficient complement to existing sustainable FL techniques.
## Significance By decoupling model size from energy allocation, this work opens a new design axis for environmentally sustainable FL systems, enabling finer-grained energy management across heterogeneous participants. Future research may focus on adaptive partition-point selection and joint optimization of latency, energy, and carbon emissions.

item.title: Hybrid Quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Privacy-Aware Federated Biosignal Learning
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces a **Hybrid Quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (HQKAN)** for privacy-aware federated ECG classification, addressing client-side data scarcity, label imbalance, and non-IID distributions.
## Method & Results Under federated averaging (FedAvg), HQKAN was benchmarked against a multilayer perceptron (MLP) on MIT-BIH (5-class) and INCART (3-class) datasets. Across multiple client configurations, HQKAN improved most aggregate and minority-class metrics while using **37.35% fewer trainable parameters** (MIT-BIH) and **44.81% fewer** (INCART), with corresponding communication cost reductions of **24.89%** and **36.41%**.
## Significance HQKAN offers a compact, communication-efficient, and robust alternative to MLP for privacy-preserving biosignal learning, effectively mitigating cross-client distribution shifts and class imbalance in federated settings.

item.title: Federated Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework, Empirical Analysis, and Future Directions
item.description:
**Federated Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework, Empirical Analysis, and Future Directions**
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of federated prompt learning (FPL), an emerging paradigm integrating federated learning with large language models (LLMs) for privacy-preserving training and inference. We systematically analyze FPL across the full model lifecycle—pre-training, fine-tuning, and applications—addressing three research questions: (1) its fundamental motivations, characteristics, and distinctions from conventional FL and full-model fine-tuning; (2) trade-offs among performance, communication efficiency, computational overhead, scalability, personalization, and heterogeneity handling; and (3) remaining security, privacy, robustness, and system challenges with defense mechanisms. We conclude by highlighting open problems and future directions, offering a unified framework to guide ongoing FPL research.

item.title: Equivalence Between Average-Case Hardness of Learning and Cryptography for Mixed Quantum States
item.description:
## Core Contribution We prove that **average-case hardness of learning (AHL) for mixed quantum states** is **equivalent** to the existence of **inefficiently verifiable one-way state generators (IV-OWSGs)**. This resolves the open question left by prior work on pure states and establishes a direct link between mixed-state AHL and EFI pairs.
## Key Consequences - **Corollary 1**: Mixed-state AHL ⇔ IV-OWSGs ⇒ connection to EFI pairs, unifying the cryptographic landscape for quantum state learning. - **Corollary 2**: Combined with existing results, we obtain a **separation between IV-OWSGs and OWSGs** relative to the SWAP oracle, highlighting a structural distinction between verifiable and non-verifiable one-way state primitives.
## Technical Highlights The proof introduces a novel technique to handle mixed states—**indistinguishability of ensemble decompositions**—which overcomes the lack of unique purification in the mixed-state setting. Both directions (AHL→IV-OWSG and IV-OWSG→AHL) are established via reductions that leverage quantum channel distances and statistical distance conversions.
## Significance This equivalence provides a unified foundation for quantum cryptographic assumptions, bridging learning theory and cryptography for mixed states, and opens avenues for exploring verifiable variants and connections to classical assumptions like LWE.

item.title: Concurrently Secure Compact Blind Signatures from Module-SIS
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present a novel lattice-based blind signature scheme that **eliminates zero-knowledge proofs** by redesigning the classical Σ-protocol (Ducas et al., CRYPTO 2013), where the final protocol message naturally forms a short preimage of the message hash (GPV-style signature). This yields a **4.7 KB signature**, nearly 5× smaller than the previous best (≥22 KB).
## Security & Efficiency The scheme achieves **concurrent security** under the Module-SIS assumption. Due to rejection sampling, it may occasionally require extra rounds; however, honest users complete in **1.1 expected rounds**, while malicious users are forced to terminate within **2.6 rounds** via a failure-proofing mechanism. This work provides the first practical compact blind signature without ZK proofs, offering a new paradigm for post-quantum blind signatures in bandwidth-constrained applications.

item.title: A Hybrid Post-Quantum Encryption Architecture with Self-Hosted Key Management for SME Cloud Data Protection
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **Quantum Cloud Guard (QCG)**, the first SME-oriented software-only architecture combining **client-side hybrid post-quantum encryption** (AES-256-GCM sealed under ML-KEM-1024), **self-hosted key custody with client-verifiable ML-DSA-87 signatures** on served keys, and an **integrated application-layer abuse-prevention gateway**. The design ensures files never leave the client unencrypted, and enterprises retain sole control of key material—separating key custody from data custody to eliminate single-provider read access.
## Key Results On a 24 MHz STM32F407, ML-KEM-1024 key generation and decapsulation take 40.8 ms and 44.0 ms respectively; server-side post-quantum operations remain sub-millisecond (signing adds 0.24 ms/request). The full service runs on a €4.49/month virtual server. Under sustained flooding, the in-process Sentinel Gate rejected 98.8% of attack traffic while legitimate median latency shifted only from 621 ms to 625 ms. QCG demonstrates that practical, verifiable post-quantum protection is achievable for SMEs at negligible cost and without external trust dependencies.

item.title: Hell’s Bells: A Neural Network Pipeline for Ternary Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms
item.description: This paper introduces a neural network-based pipeline that automatically generates fast matrix multiplication (FMM) algorithms for small but arbitrary dimensions $(n,m,k)$. The network is tunable, enabling the production of schemes with desirable practical properties such as ternary coefficients, sparsity, and low post-optimization addition counts. Through generating and optimizing thousands of algorithms, the authors demonstrate clear performance gains across the entire FMM pipeline. They achieve record-low additive complexity for several dimension combinations, particularly excelling at $(2,2,k)$ with improvements that grow with $k$. Notably, they show that minimizing additions during generation can be suboptimal for the overall pipeline, revealing structural FMM properties. All code, generated schemes, and datasets are publicly released.

item.title: Theoretical Open Problems in Symmetric Cryptography: Verifiable LLM-Guided Analysis
item.description: We introduce the **Pilot–Sailor Framework**, an LLM-guided system for tackling theoretical open problems in symmetric cryptography. Pilot generates intermediate lemmas and proof strategies, while Sailor constructs formal proofs that must pass machine verification in a proof assistant, ensuring all admitted results are fully checked. Applied across fourteen case studies in Boolean-function theory and cryptanalysis, we achieve complete resolutions, corrected formulations, counterexamples, and quantitative advances. Key results include: a full proof of the pointwise Tu–Deng conjecture for all word lengths, with an exact equality characterization based on zero-gap distances; a new upper bound \(\operatorname{NL}(F)\leq2^{n-1}-2^{n/2-1}-2\) for mappings from \(\mathbb F_2^n\) to \(\mathbb F_2^m\) under specified conditions; and a computer-assisted proof that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in eight variables is 116, ruling out 118. Ten additional open questions are also resolved. This work demonstrates a viable paradigm for AI-guided, formally verifiable mathematical research.

item.title: A Unifying Umbrella for Circular-Secure Cryptographic Primitives
item.description:
## Key Contribution This paper establishes **existential equivalence** among seemingly distinct circular-secure primitives, unifying them under a new conceptual framework.
## Main Results - **Equivalence breakthrough**: Hinting PRGs (CRYPTO 2019) are proven equivalent to key-dependent-message (KDM)-secure symmetric encryption (SKE). - **New notion**: We introduce **key-dependent-shift (KDS) security** for weak PRFs, serving as a central hub that connects all circular-style primitives. - **Extended equivalence**: KDS-secure weak PRFs also imply linear-resistant PRGs (ITC 2023) and hinting weak PRFs (ASIACRYPT 2022), making all these primitives mutually equivalent. - **Novel applications**: KDS security enables new constructions of RDM-secure public-key encryption and correlated-product secure trapdoor functions.
## Technical Core The central technical result is a **generic construction of KDS-secure weak PRFs from any KDM-secure SKE**, bridging symmetric encryption and circular-security.
## Significance This work provides a **unifying umbrella** for circular-secure cryptography, simplifying future design and proof efforts.

item.title: Pruning Merkle-Tree Consistent Accumulator
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces **pruning accumulators**, a novel stateful authenticated data structure supporting both incremental addition of new elements and pruning of expired old prefixes. The digest represents only the unpruned sequence while maintaining full functionality (inclusion proofs, proof updates, consistency checks) for remaining elements—ideal for sliding-window authenticated applications.
## Technical Approach Two Merkle-tree-based constructions are proposed, both achieving efficient accumulation, prefix pruning, proof generation/updating, and verification while preserving standard Merkle-tree verification style for active elements and reducing long-term storage.
## Results & Validation The work provides formal definitions, rigorous correctness and security proofs, an open-source implementation, and experimental evaluation demonstrating significant performance gains from pruning. This addresses a critical gap in append-only systems like Certificate Transparency where expired elements cannot be removed.

item.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **AutoDesign**, a framework that treats multimodal summarization (e.g., paper-to-poster) as a long-horizon agentic process. A **meta-harness optimizer** guides a code agent to recursively improve the harness system based on rollout feedback, aligning with human design priors while accumulating reusable experience.
## Key Results - On our new **PosterBench** benchmark (100 papers, five disciplines), AutoDesign scores **78.32**, surpassing the commercial system Claude Design by **7.45 points**. - Across seven controlled configurations, integrating the learned DesignHarness boosts average score from **54.99 to 67.39 (+12.4%)**. - In a fully autonomous loop, it completes 253 tool calls and 11 editing turns in 40 minutes for under **$3**, achieving conference-poster quality per human evaluation. - A system-blind study shows AutoDesign receives the highest human preference among all evaluated systems.
## Significance AutoDesign demonstrates that recursive, experience-driven harness optimization significantly outperforms static pipelines, offering a cost-effective, self-improving paradigm for long-horizon agentic design tasks.

item.title: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **OmniScientist**, an end-to-end omni-modal AI scientist that conducts multidisciplinary research directly from heterogeneous raw evidence (images, signals, audio, video, 3D structures, trajectories, tables, formulae, graphs). Unlike prior systems relying on text or precomputed summaries, it integrates a perception layer and three autonomous agents (ideation, experiment, writeup) within a deterministic pipeline, enabling lifecycle-wide perception where observations continuously shape research questions, experimental decisions, and final claims. Built-in code-level checks enforce novelty, statistical validity, execution provenance, and numerical traceability.
## Key Results Evaluated on 36 real-data cases across 5 discipline families, the system completed the full raw-data-to-manuscript pipeline in all cases, achieving a mean paper score of 6.3. In paired comparisons against a blind variant using precomputed scalar features, direct perception improved all 7 evaluation dimensions and won 85% of head-to-head judgments.
## Significance These findings demonstrate that lifecycle-wide perception is essential for evidence-grounded discovery, offering a practical path toward broadly capable AI scientists.

item.title: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
item.description: We introduce **Vero**, the first benchmark for evaluating joint implementation and proof synthesis at the repository level. It comprises 43 multi-module instances from real-world projects (Python, Dafny, Verus, Coq) spanning cryptographic protocols and distributed systems, each requiring Lean 4 code with formal specifications and supporting both proof-only and code-and-proof modes. A unique audit mechanism lets agents formally prove specification unsatisfiability or reference-code incorrectness, enhancing benchmark reliability. Evaluating frontier coding agents with Lean toolchain access, the strongest agent solves only 27/43 instances and closes no specifications on hardest repos, revealing a substantial gap in repository-scale verified software synthesis. Vero provides a concrete testbed for tracking progress; benchmark, pipeline, and harness are publicly released.

item.title: The data geometry of masking diffusion: Certified-optimal schedules via unmasking growth complexity
item.description:
## Core Contribution This paper introduces the **unmasking growth complexity (UGC)**, a path-resolved measure of data geometry for masking diffusion, whose local increments directly govern KL discretization error. This yields a unified analysis of Bernoulli-subset and fixed-cardinality unmasking schemes, and enables optimized single- and multi-block schedules in log-reveal-odds coordinates.
## Key Innovation The authors show UGC increments can be estimated from samples via KL increments along coupled reveal trajectories, leading to **certified-optimal samplers** that achieve prescribed KL error with high probability and iteration complexity within a constant factor of the oracle procedure.
## Main Results Collapsing the UGC path links to classical multivariate dependence measures. In the fine-partition limit, the squared integral of the square-root UGC density determines the sharp leading-order optimal Euler discretization error. Examples demonstrate substantial dimension-dependent gains, including $\widetilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{d})$ improvements with a constant number of adaptive blocks.

item.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data
item.description:
## Core Contribution We introduce **Mimir v1**, a 1-billion-parameter language model based on the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM) architecture, trained **exclusively on permissible post-training data** (161 public datasets) without any non-compliant pre-training corpus.
## Key Results - **Outperforms same-scale baseline** (HRM-Text 1B) across 20 benchmarks covering English, Math & Code, and Danish. - **Competes with larger models**: matches or exceeds Qwen 3.5 4B and Gemma 4 E2B on multiple tasks, demonstrating exceptional parameter efficiency. - **New SOTA for Danish**, providing a strong open-source tool for low-resource language communities.
## Significance This work proves that a small model, paired with a carefully curated compliance-first data strategy and an efficient reasoning architecture, can deliver frontier-level practical performance—lowering the barrier for ethical, reproducible LLM research. The model is fully open-sourced on Hugging Face Hub.

item.title: AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling - Full Technical Report (v1.1)
item.description:
## Key Contribution AlayaWorld v1.1 revises the conditioning mechanism for interactive long-horizon world modeling while keeping the backbone architecture, chunk-wise autoregressive generation, and training data unchanged.
## Core Changes Guided by the principle that **conditioning signals should match generated content in both latent representation and temporal structure**, we introduce two major architectural shifts: (1) replacing depth-warping-based spatial memory with a **streaming 3D point-cache renderer**, and (2) encoding all visual conditions in the **same causal-VAE latent space** as the generated video.
## Six Specific Modifications - Motion-aware latent conditioning instead of static-frame conditioning - Continuous causal encoding of re-rendered spatial memory - Pixel-space alignment of temporal memory windows - Hard memory dropout (token removal, not zeroing) - Unified VAE encoding/decoding across training and inference - Removal of the camera AdaLN branch—viewpoint control relies solely on the re-rendered spatial condition
## Impact These changes achieve tighter alignment between conditioning and generation, improving multi-view consistency and temporal coherence for long-horizon interactive video synthesis.

item.title: MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
item.description:
## MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
We present **MARC (Multi-Agent Reasoning and Coordination)**, an open-source framework that replaces monolithic LLM prompting with deterministic multi-agent orchestration for clinical reasoning. MARC coordinates four role-specialized agents—extraction, reasoning, answer generation, and evaluation—with explicit context passing and traceable intermediate outputs, enabling stage-wise failure attribution. A novel **Decomposer** module automatically generates task-specific agent prompts from plain-language descriptions, eliminating manual prompt engineering. The framework supports both API-based and local CPU-compatible deployments, is fully configurable via YAML without code changes, and is model-agnostic, interpretable, and accessible to clinical experts without programming skills. MARC is publicly available at https://github.com/Penn-RAIL/MARC-v1.

item.title: AaLLM: An End-to-End Analog Circuit Design Framework from Topology Generation to Sizing Using Large Language Models
item.description:
## Core Contribution We present **AaLLM**, an open-source end-to-end multi-agent LLM framework for analog circuit design. It directly maps user specifications to a complete netlist, integrating both topology generation and circuit sizing in a single pipeline.
## Key Innovations - **Automated knowledge base** built from papers/textbooks, eliminating manual data collection. - **RAG-based expertise emulation** for circuit design reasoning. - **Tri-agent feedback loop** (Designer-Critic-Evaluator) that reduces sizing iterations via arbitration.
## Results AaLLM generates novel topologies with figure-of-merit (FoM) comparable to known designs, up to **3× higher** for certain circuits. It achieves **3–4.5× fewer SPICE calls** at inference and **40× lower wall-clock time** versus state-of-the-art multi-agent LLM pipelines. This work demonstrates a fully automated, efficient alternative to conventional analog design workflows.

item.title: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models
item.description:
**Core Contribution**: This study tackles concept drift in malware classification by comparing three drift detection techniques—novel One-Class SVM (OCSVM), Minibatch K-Means (MK-Means), and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)—across four classifiers (MLP, RF, SVM, XGBoost).
**Key Results**: Under a drift-aware retraining policy, all detection methods achieve accuracy comparable to periodic retraining while requiring substantially fewer model updates. The OCSVM-based approach generally outperforms MK-Means and MMD in both accuracy and training efficiency. Pareto front analysis confirms a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.
**Conclusion**: Lightweight drift detection enables reliable, resource-efficient malware model maintenance, with OCSVM emerging as the most robust choice for real-world deployment.
